A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftTreeMax research despite the changed title. Their main texts, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-MDP variance calculations in Figure 1 and Atari reward, gradient-variance and training results in Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-MDP results and Atari experiments in Figures 1, 3, 5 and 6, including results retained from v1.

M1.justification: Equation 2 introduces a gamma^(-d) multiplier on trajectory logits, also reflected in Algorithm 1. This changes policy and gradient scaling at fixed temperature, but retains the cumulative and exponentiated variants, tree expansion, leaf network and PPO integration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight Atari games and synthetic MDPs with near-uniform, random and near-permutation transitions. The approximate-model extension in v2 is theoretical; it does not introduce an evaluated learned-model or continuous-control scenario.

E2.justification: Distributed PPO remains the plotted baseline. However, v2 Section 6 additionally reports an empirical comparison of E-SoftTreeMax with C-SoftTreeMax, finding almost identical results; v1 explicitly left empirical E-SoftTreeMax testing to future work.

E3.justification: v1 Figure 4 specifies a 200-million-step cap and a one-week limit, with PPO finishing earlier. v2 Figures 5–6 instead describe one-week runs with varying step counts and add evaluation against online interactions, excluding tree-expansion interactions. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing depth sweeps and synthetic-transition analyses remain. v2 adds a qualitative comparison of the two SoftTreeMax variants and an analysis of depth-dependent sample efficiency using online-interaction curves in Appendix B.5, extending the earlier wall-clock analysis.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging and training-curve standard deviations are retained. However, v2 drops v1 Section 4.2's disclosure that multiple synthetic-MDP experiments were conducted and only one instance was shown. This removes limited replication information without establishing that fewer runs occurred.

E6.justification: The learning-curve evidence is substantially revised: v2 Figure 5 contains changed PPO curves relative to v1 Figure 4, and Figure 6 adds interaction-indexed results across all eight games. Figure 1 also has different variance traces, and a qualitative C/E comparison is added. Figure 3 is identical; the revisions do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 introduces discounted state-visitation definitions, revises gradients and variance bounds for the normalized logits, and removes the earlier infinite-depth Boltzmann-limit statement. Section 4.3 and Appendix A.9 add model-misspecification definitions, lemmas and a C-SoftTreeMax gradient-bias bound. Theorem 4.7 also extends its stated eigenvalue-rate special case to reversible transitions.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add a central claim that approximate forward models yield gradient bias controlled by model error while retaining variance reduction, including a claimed first such guarantee. The preferred-transition description changes from uniformity to state independence. The three-orders-of-magnitude variance reduction and up-to-fivefold reward claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of the depth-dependent bias–variance tradeoff, temperature selection and nonuniform gradient shrinkage. Appendix C.1 qualifies the zero-variance ideal by explaining that the gradient can also vanish and learning stall. New limitations and Appendix B.5 discuss stochastic environments, GPU dependence and game-specific failures of deeper planning.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promise of a future code release with a reported repository and Docker/README guidance. Appendix B adds GPU batching and pruning details, policy and PPO pseudocode, and the GAE parameter of 0.95. These substantially expand reproducibility information; existing hardware, worker and width settings are largely relocated.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops distinctions from n-step TD, GAE, natural policy gradients and lookahead policy mirror descent, including Protopapas and Barakat (2024). It also reworks the relationship to conventional tree search around exhaustive expansion and parallel or learned models, with additions and removals of cited works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related-work narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten. Experimental details and training-curve discussion move into a structured Appendix B, the E-SoftTreeMax proof outline moves into Appendix A, and a dedicated reproducibility/limitations section is introduced.

P2.justification: v2 adds a GPU-expansion diagram, online-interaction plots and two algorithm displays. It enlarges and relocates the policy schematic, moves the time-based training plots to the appendix, and redesigns Figure 1's colors, line styles, legend and scale. Figure 3 remains visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves implementation documentation and adds useful model-error theory and online-interaction analysis. However, the new logit scaling changes v1's depth-independent lower bound in Appendix A.1.8, Equation 33, into a bound that can vanish with depth in v2 Appendix A.8, Equation 31. The proof nevertheless invokes a fixed exponential contraction. This leaves a central revised variance guarantee unsupported by the displayed argument, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
